- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.10) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, cap peak forecast at 10–15% below true peak.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤ -0.10) and price is trending down, model often underestimates; add 2–5% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- Model frequently underestimates true mean in 30-day horizon when sentiment is volatile or mixed; apply slight upward bias (1–3%) to mean forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows recent reversal (e.g., from negative to positive), model often lags; adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect sentiment shift.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if model’s first 5–7 days are significantly below true, apply upward correction to early period (e.g., +1–2% per day).  
- When sentiment is weak or flat, model tends to overfit recent noise; smooth forecast by averaging last 3–5 days’ values.
